# Cuts and seams

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

How one shot becomes the next: carried cuts, hard cuts on sound, flashes, defocus and blank-frame seams. 34 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Anchored overlay, background swap

`tr-anchor-overlay-cut` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough, loop, vertical

A foreground element (a pin, a status pill, a modal, a big word) keeps its exact screen position while the world behind it hard-cuts, so a total change of scene reads as a change of zoom or context.

- **Build:** Render the overlay from one absolute-frame function drawn by every act it crosses (deviceAt in references/transitions.md §4.1). Use the identical transform string on both sides of each cut, so its last frame in one act and its first in the next are consecutive samples of one curve. Each background change is an act boundary; a montage is 2-3 background acts in a row behind the same overlay. The overlay keeps its own clock through the cut (a running scale tween, a 0.5-1 px/f drift or a breath() push), so it is never static for more than 48 f. After the last swap the overlay acts on the new world: it travels into its slot on E.glide over 40 f (moves up to 350 px), or FLIPs into an input.
- **Timing:** Background holds of 10-22 f each in a montage (2-3 swaps), or a single swap. Overlay offset across the cut: 0 px ideally, 30 px at most. Overlay drift 0.5-1 px/f. Follow-up move 40 f on E.glide. Cuts on beats or 16ths.
- **Use when:** Showing that one thing persists across contexts: a location going from 3D city to map, a request going from an empty void to the full app, a claim held over a run of photos.
- **Avoid when:** The overlay is text that must be reread after each swap, or the backgrounds are busy and bright enough to swallow it. Keep backgrounds near 5% mean luma under light overlays.

### Angle change on a shared drift

`tr-drift-matched-angle-cut` · transitions · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, loop

A hard cut jumps to a new angle or the next state of the same object (front to top-down, open to closed) while the slow zoom or pan carries on at exactly the same rate, so a calm shot changes viewpoint with no jolt and no speed ramp.

- **Build:** Write the drift once as a function of the absolute frame and multiply it into both acts' anchor-camera k (src/lib/camera.ts): d(abs) = lmix(1.10, 1, prog(abs, a, a + 96, E.outSoft)) for a settling pull (lmix(1, 1.10, ...) for a push), plus any pan as sx += v · (abs − a). zoomSpeed(kA, cut − 1) then equals zoomSpeed(kB, cut) by construction. Shot A frames the subject from one angle. Shot B frames the same subject at least 30 deg away (yaw ±35-50 deg on a tilted UI plane, or a top-down pitch on an object built with depth) or in its next state (lid open to closed, card face to back). Its on-screen centre stays within ±40 px of A's and its apparent size within ±15%. Cut on an act boundary 8-16 f into the drift, on a beat, while the frame still changes about 0.3% per frame. When the subject itself acts (a lid closes, a device turns), drive that action from one absolute progress too and cut at 35-55% of it, so it finishes in the new angle. Keep the stage colour and light identical, and add no ghost frame.
- **Timing:** Drift 96 f on E.outSoft from 1.10x (or a 2-4 px/f pan). Cut 8-16 f in, at −0.26 to −0.36% scale per frame (about 3 px/f at the frame edge); the drift settles 40-80 f after the cut. Angle change at least 30 deg, centre offset at most 40 px, size change at most 15%. Optional subject action 36-60 f on E.smooth, cut at 35-55% of it. Cut in 0 f.
- **Use when:** Calm films and product beauty shots where a velocity ramp would be too loud: showing an object's second side or its next state within one continuous gesture.
- **Avoid when:** The two angles look alike (under about 30 deg it reads as a jump cut), the subject's size or position jumps, or one side is static. For a lift in energy, use a velocity handoff instead.

### Conveyor line swap

`tr-conveyor-line-swap` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, vertical, loop

The current line floats up and fades, the stage is empty for an instant, and the next line rises from below into the same spot, so a run of statements reads as one upward feed.

- **Build:** Outgoing line: translateY 0 → −135 px through depart(q), with q = prog(f, 0, 30, E.in); opacity 1 → 0 over its last 8 f, plus blurOut(q, 8). Leave 2 empty frames. Incoming line: translateY +188 → 0 through arrive(p), with p = prog(f, 0, 30, E.out). Its opacity goes 0 → 1 over the first 10 f, so it flies faded while faster than 20 px/f, and its colour goes C.mute → C.ink over 16 f with mixColor. For a word-by-word version, use Words.tsx with stagger 3-4 and out/outDur 16, so each old word rises away as its replacement rises in. Keep one direction (up) for the whole run.
- **Timing:** Exit: 30 f on E.in (last frame about 26 px/f, while fading). Gap 2 f. Entry: 30 f on E.out (first frame about 37 px/f, while faded); colour over 16 f. Per-word stagger 3-4 f. One line per bar or half bar.
- **Use when:** Sequences of short claims, lists of capabilities, a subject that changes while the predicate stays.
- **Avoid when:** Lines of very different length or alignment (the eye loses the slot), or more than 4-5 lines in a row without another seam type.

### Cut tighter mid-move, same vector

`dv-punch-in-cut` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · any

A hard cut to a 1.16-2.5x closer framing of the same thing, inside a continuing move: the content keeps moving the same way and decelerates, or the close-up pulls back 9 % on a decay, or just creeps on; a jump cut can skip forward inside an expansion.

- **Build:** handoffShot with a scale factor (carry x, y); SnapZoom with pre: 0 for the one-frame version. Anatomy: Scale step 1.16-2.5x on the cut; the motion vector continues; decay or creep after; two one-frame punch-ins can coexist with two marker sets. Sound: On the beat (+40 ms) or a keypress just before.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Settle 30-70 f (34 % in the first 10 %); creep 0.4-0.6 %/f.
- **Use when:** Emphasis on a word, a field, a button while the action continues.
- **Avoid when:** Cutting to the same scale (a jump cut that reads as a mistake).

### Defocus cut through one empty frame

`tr-defocus-cut` · transitions · workhorse · energy calm · launch, update, walkthrough · also `dv-defocus-blank-cut`

A line blurs out and fades together, one empty frame, and the next line arrives very soft and pulls into focus while it types on.

- **Build:** <DefocusCut frame at={emptyFrame} out in outgoing incoming ground /> (out / in time the blur, outgoing / incoming are the lines).
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.DefocusCut`, `fx/CutFx.defocusCutState`
- **Timing:** Out 18 f to 32 px at 1080p on E.buildIn with the fade on the same clock; 1 empty frame; in from 45 px, x0.80 per 60 fps frame (x0.65 at 30), sharp after 18 f.
- **Use when:** Between two statements, on a breath in the music.
- **Avoid when:** Fast cuts on hits (it is a quiet device).

### Path relay

`tr-path-relay` · transitions · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, loop

A line and its lead dot carry the eye from one place to the next. The connector bends around a rounded corner with the camera following, or continues across a cut and enters the next shot from the same edge at the same angle.

- **Build:** Draw the connector as an SVG path (stroke ≥ 1.5 px, C.white on ink or C.ink on paper) with pathLength 1, revealed by stroke-dashoffset; corners are arcs of r = 40 px. Place the lead dot with getPointAtLength (from @remotion/paths, or an analytic line-plus-arc), where the arc length grows with prog(f, a, b, E.linear) at 8-16 px/f. The camera follows with a lag: the anchor-camera Shot frames the dot's position at f − 10. Across a cut, start shot B's path at the frame edge where A's path left, at the same angle and speed, so the dot reaches its target 18 f after the cut. Off-frame variant: the dot or cursor speeds out of frame on E.contact over 24 f and stays hidden 12 f while the camera relocates. It then re-enters at ≤ 60 px/f, slowing ×0.92 per frame to rest in about 36 f.
- **Timing:** Dot at a constant 8-16 px/f. Corner radius 40 px. Camera lag 8-12 f. One run lasts 60-72 f. After a cut the dot lands 18 f later. Off-frame gap 12 f; re-entry at ≤ 60 px/f, slowing ×0.92 per frame.
- **Use when:** Money, data or messages travelling (send, route, sync), flowcharts and timelines, and films whose UI already uses lines and nodes.
- **Avoid when:** The film has no line language, or the path would cross readable text. A path that loops back reads as indecision.

### Tip-back exit

`tr-tip-back-exit` · transitions · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

The outgoing scene tips away from camera like a sheet laid onto a table, or flips up into a line, speeding up and fading into the next stage colour, and the next element lands on the clean field.

- **Build:** Wrap the outgoing scene in a 3D container (transform-origin 50% 100%, perspective 1200 px) and tip it: rotateX 0 → 40 deg and translateY 0 → +10% over 30 f on E.smooth. Lay a floor of the stage colour over it, opaque across the bottom 25% and transparent from 55% up, so the scene sinks into the stage, and dim it toward the next act's stage colour (overlay 0 → 0.9) over the last 12 f. Fast version: rotateX 0 → 88 deg with translateY 0 → −400 px over 20 f on E.contact (last frame about 70 px/f), so the scene flattens into a line at the top edge and uncovers what sits beneath. Flat version: a clip-path inset from the bottom grows on E.contact over 24 f, and the cut lands on its fastest frame. The next element starts on the frame the exit clears, or 1 f before.
- **Timing:** Tip-back: 30 f on E.smooth (rotateX 40 deg). Flip to a line: 20 f on E.contact. Crop collapse: 24 f on E.contact. Dim overlay 0 → 0.9 over the last 12 f. The next element starts 0-1 f after the exit clears.
- **Use when:** Ending a UI section to hand over to a statement or an alert, when the next beat needs an empty stage for big type.
- **Avoid when:** The next act opens on the same pose (use a relay instead), or the dim would go to black and back up (a dip) instead of into the next stage colour.

### Velocity handoff cut

`tr-velocity-handoff-cut` · transitions · workhorse · energy any · any · also `dv-velocity-handoff-cut`

The outgoing shot speeds up in one direction and is cut on its fastest frame. The next shot opens already moving the same way and brakes to rest, so momentum runs straight through the edit.

- **Build:** Make the cut an act boundary in timeline.ts so motion-blur samples never straddle it, and place it on a beat with b(). In the outgoing act, drive the camera (src/lib/camera.ts) or the hero's translate on E.exit (E.contact, or E.in for a harder snap) over its last 16-24 f, so it ends at peak speed on the final frame; for a zoom, apply the same ramp to k through lmix. In the incoming act, start the key element moving on frame 0 in the same screen direction at 1.0-1.5x that speed and slow it on E.out over 45-90 f. Size the two sides with exitSpeed(D, T, ease) and entryDistance(v, T) from references/transitions.md; for a flicked list, use y = v0·(1 − k^f)/(1 − k) with k = 0.92-0.943 and no overshoot. Give each act one dominant screen vector (+x in one act, −x in the next) and start every incoming element on the side it would enter from.
- **Primitive:** `lib/handoff.handoffShot`, `lib/handoff.carry`, `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Exit: last 16-24 f on E.exit (speed grows about ×1.1-1.2 per frame), ending at 25-40 px/f (never above 60) or −6 to −8% scale per frame. Entry: 30-55 px/f on frame 0, slowing about ×0.92-0.94 per frame (E.out over 45-90 f; entryDistance(40, 60) is about 400 px). A 1-3 px/f drift may run under the hold before the ramp. Text inside a moving shot must be under 20 px/f by the time it has to be read.
- **Use when:** Most cuts between moving shots: feature-to-feature edits, montages, chapter changes, and any film that must never stop. Velocity-matched cuts are exempt from the two-uses-per-type limit.
- **Avoid when:** One side has to be still (a held statement or a designed freeze), or the two shots would move in opposite directions. Carry a shape or an anchor across instead.

### Block step and silhouette

`tr-block-step` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, vertical · also `dv-block-silhouette-step`

Two flat blocks cover the old frame one frame each, then the incoming element appears as a flat silhouette of itself and steps back to the real thing in three even steps.

- **Build:** <BlockStep frame at blocks={[rectA, rectB]} silhouette={{ rect: incomingBox, decay: 3 }} outgoing incoming />; declares its flashes and stepped frames.
- **Primitive:** `fx/BlockStep.BlockStep`, `fx/BlockStep.blockStepState`
- **Materials:** The incoming page arrives as a pure white rectangle, then decays through grey to its real dark self one step a frame (white overlay opacity 1, 0.65, 0.35, 0, no easing between), landing on a VO syllable; a 2 px white rim light with a soft glow brightest at the bottom-left keeps the page's edge lit from below.
- **Timing:** 1 frame per block, the silhouette at 1, 2/3, 1/3, 0 over three frames; on a hit.
- **Use when:** A hard beat with nothing to carry across it.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films; more than twice a film; never in the accent colour.

### Cut through exactly one blank frame

`dv-one-blank-frame` · transitions · accent · energy calm · any

A hard cut through exactly one empty frame (black, pure white, or the brand's background colour) separates two sections like a breath.

- **Build:** blackDipState({ black: 1, fadeUp: 0 }) or a one-frame flat Sequence. Anatomy: One full frame of a flat colour. Sound: Between voice words, or a shutter click and a drum just after. Materials: A panel can start from one empty frame of its ground (2 f) before the first block, again before a loop restart.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.blackDipState`
- **Materials:** A panel can start from one empty frame of its ground (2 f) before the first block, again before a loop restart.
- **Timing:** 1 f at the film rate (2-3 f at 60 fps).
- **Use when:** Between story and finale; a section break inside a voice-led film.
- **Avoid when:** More than one per minute; two frames (that reads as a glitch).

### Full blur straight into a near-static calm shot

`dv-speed-contrast-cut` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, feature

From a 6800 px/s smear on white, cut straight to a calm, sharp, full-bleed landscape with a small tagline; the frame before the blur cut can show the outgoing scene sharp in an earlier position, a frozen anchor before the smear.

- **Build:** Scroll or whip at peak speed with the blur pass on its frames, cut to a Photo with a 0.3 px/f drift. Anatomy: Blur at peak speed on the last frames; one sharp anchor frame; the calm shot barely moving. Sound: The blur's whoosh cut dead by the calm shot.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Cut on the grid (+120 ms vs the beat).
- **Use when:** Contrast between product speed and a calm promise.
- **Avoid when:** Blending the two speeds.

### Horizon rise

`tr-horizon-rise` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A huge disc rises from the bottom edge like a planet horizon, its rim washing over the frame, until its dark core swallows the screen and becomes the stage for the next line.

- **Build:** One full-frame layer holds a circle of radius R = 1.1 × frame width (2112 px at 1080p), centred horizontally: a dark core in the next act's stage colour out to 55% of R, then bands of rim colour out to 85%, softened by a 30 px blur. In the full look the rim is several hues with a bloom. Bake the disc as a dithered PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py so the soft falloff does not band. Move its centre from y = H + R (the disc's top just touching the bottom edge) to y = 0.58 H over 56 f on E.dolly, with the previous scene disappearing behind it; at rest the core covers all four corners. Start the next text at about frame 46, inside the core. Lighter version: a rim band 40% of the frame height rises from the bottom edge over 16 f on E.in, and the cut lands mid-rise on the beat.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep one hue: the dark core, then a rim of the accent at full strength falling off by opacity of that same accent (no second hue, no bloom), baked dithered. Or use a hard-edged ink disc with a 1.5 px accent edge rising over a paper stage. The full look relies on gradient, glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Rise: 56 f on E.dolly, about 2570 px of centre travel at 1080p (the rim's leading edge peaks near 70 px/f mid-move). Next text from about frame 46. Band version: 16 f on E.in. The core fills the frame on a downbeat.
- **Use when:** A single colour event that divides the film into acts (UI section to brand moment), or a calm lift from a statement into the next card.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film, or on a light film where the dark core would be the only dark frame.

### Line parts from the middle, layout swaps on frame three

`dv-line-split-swap` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, feature

The two halves of a title move apart from the middle (7 px, then 31-38 px) and on the third frame the whole layout is replaced.

- **Build:** doorSplitState(f, { start, frames: 6 at 60 fps, rise: false }) on the title layer only (the measured door path: each step about x1.5 the last; no card rises), swap on its third frame. Anatomy: Ease-in split; swap on frame 3. Sound: An orchestral stab.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.doorSplitState`
- **Timing:** 6 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** A quick change of scene from a centred title.
- **Avoid when:** Long splits (the swap must come early).

### Next scene's tiles fly over the outgoing shot

`dv-overlap-tiles-cut` · transitions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Tiles of the next scene fly into the frame over the outgoing card a few frames before the cut; or the old panels hold 1-3 frames over the new photo, then blank tiles re-tile into the new layout and fill.

- **Build:** Cards enterState per tile starting 8 f before the cut; HardStep holds for the overlap. Anatomy: Tiles settle expo (34 % on the first moving frame); overlap 4 f; re-tile 12 f, fill 12-20 f. Sound: An onset at the tiles; speech then a glockenspiel.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Cards`
- **Timing:** 38-108 f.
- **Use when:** Grid-based films; image-led sequences.
- **Avoid when:** Tiles that do not belong to the next scene.

### One block stamped into a plus of five

`dv-stamp-replicate` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, feature

On one frame the loader block is replicated into a plus of five blocks (each in a different phase of its animation) at 58 % scale, which then pulse smaller twice.

- **Build:** HardStep the copies on one frame; each copy's animation offset by a phase. Anatomy: One-frame stamp; pulses -15 % then -11 % expo-out. Sound: An orchestral stab (+10 ms).
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** Stamp 1 f; pulses 22 f each.
- **Use when:** A loader or icon multiplying into many.
- **Avoid when:** Without a loop-able element to replicate.

### One or two inverted frames between shots

`dv-inverted-flash-frame` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, sting

Between two shots, one frame of the scene (or two frames of the key word) appears with its colours inverted: black type on the accent, white on black.

- **Build:** HardStep a one-frame layer with filter invert(1) (or a pre-built inverted card). Anatomy: Inverted colours on one or two frames; the key word alone, centred. Sound: A chat pop. Materials: The flash frame can already carry the next scene's geometry (a dashed circle split by a line, two faint perspective lines) that only arrives seconds later: a seed planted in 4 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Materials:** The flash frame can already carry the next scene's geometry (a dashed circle split by a line, two faint perspective lines) that only arrives seconds later: a seed planted in 4 f.
- **Timing:** 1-2 f at the film rate.
- **Use when:** Punctuation between scenes; flashing the key word.
- **Avoid when:** Long flashes; more than two per film.

### One panel at 2x for one frame

`dv-overscale-bridge-frame` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, feature

From a four-quadrant grid, all quadrants make their last move and on the final frame one quadrant fills the frame at 2x for exactly one frame, then a hard cut.

- **Build:** HardStep the cell's scale to frame size for one frame. Anatomy: A one-frame full-frame of one cell, scaled 2x. Sound: None needed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Timing:** 1 f.
- **Use when:** Leaving a grid of shots.
- **Avoid when:** More than one frame.

### Polarity flip cut

`tr-polarity-flip-cut` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature

A hard cut flips the stage between near-black and near-white on a downbeat, often with the same icon or pill held on the same spot in inverted colours, so the luminance jump itself is the accent.

- **Build:** Plan adjacent acts with opposite stage luminance (mean luma differing by at least 150 of 255) and cut on their act boundary on a downbeat, after a dropout or silence, with one impact in the sound. Carry the flip; never cut from a static frame. Either cut on the outgoing motion peak (a zoom-through or an accelerating exit), or end on a shape centred at P and open on the same shape at P ±20 px, at 1-2.5x the size, with fill and ground swapped. An ink icon on paper becomes a paper icon on ink; an accent pill on paper becomes a paper pill on an accent field. The incoming shape is already drifting, translateY −36 px over 30 f on E.out. For a softer edge, draw two ghost frames with the incoming shot at 0.12 and then 0.94 opacity over the fully opaque outgoing frame. Declare the cut for scripts/forensics.py, and use no flash frame and no dip through black.
- **Timing:** Cut in 0 f, or 2 ghost frames at 0.12 and 0.94. Anchor scale jump 1.0-2.5x. Post-cut drift 30 f on E.out. After a flip to dark, wait 12-20 f before any small type. At most one flip per bar and two flip cuts per film.
- **Use when:** Act breaks: problem to answer, public to private, demo to claim. The strongest punctuation on a drop.
- **Avoid when:** A third time in one film; a flip from a static frame with nothing carried; or when the accent field would be the film's second full-frame accent flood.

### Scene burns out to white

`dv-burn-to-white` · transitions · accent · energy high · launch, sting

The scene over-exposes into white: a bloom ring grows while tiles fly at the camera, a collage's contrast collapses through stepped tints, or a whip pan washes to white, then a hard cut to a white page.

- **Build:** <Exposure> with up = the ramp and swap at the peak, hue white. Anatomy: Luma 173-189 -> 234-237 over 5-16 f; tints stepped every 2-3 f. Sound: The loudest moment with a crack or uplifter; a whoosh.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** The burn is white or a pale tint of the accent only. The full look relies on orange; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Exposure`
- **Timing:** 30-40 f ramp.
- **Use when:** Into a white end section; the loudest moment.
- **Avoid when:** Tinted burns outside the brand colour.

### Select and retype swap

`tr-select-retype-swap` · transitions · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, vertical

A finished headline is selected like text in an editor, the highlight holds for a beat, and on one frame the selection is replaced by a caret that types the next line in the same place.

- **Build:** Set both lines left-aligned in the same font, size and baseline, with line A rendered as per-character spans. The selection is a highlight rect 1.15 em tall from the ascender line: C.ink on paper with the covered glyphs switched to C.paper, or C.white with C.ink glyphs on an ink stage. Its left edge jumps one word leftward every 2-3 f, from the last word to the first, decided with fd and placed from measureTracked prefix widths; for a select-all it covers the line in one frame. The caret sits solid at its left edge. Hold the selection 10-12 f. Then, on one fd frame, remove line A and the highlight together, leave the caret at the line start and put one tick on that frame. Type line B with TypeOn from the same frame (2 f per character on E.type, head fade 4 f, caret blinking once idle). For a centred line, offset it by (full width − typed width)/2, using typeOn().followX through a 6-10 f lag. If the new line's last word is the beat that lands, give it the accent and relax it to ink over 12 f through charStyle.
- **Timing:** Selection 2-3 f per word (or a 1 f select-all), hold 10-12 f, replace on 1 f. Line B types at 2 f per character on E.type (a 20-character line in 40 f), and the caret blinks 30 f on, 30 f off once idle. About 60-75 f in all for a five-word, 20-character pair.
- **Use when:** Products where text is the medium (editors, prompts, writing and AI tools); correcting a claim, where the assumption is selected and overwritten by the answer; two or three headline swaps that should feel authored.
- **Avoid when:** The product has nothing to do with text, lines run past about 40 characters (the typing outlasts the read), or the swap repeats more than three times in a row and turns into a typing demo.

### Short fade through white between sections

`dv-white-dip-fade` · transitions · accent · energy calm · any

Section changes on a white ground use quick fades through white (10-28 f at 60 fps).

- **Build:** blackDipState with the ground colour white and fadeUp 8-14 f. Anatomy: Opacity dip to the white ground and back. Sound: Often a ding or a pluck.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.blackDipState`
- **Timing:** 10-28 f.
- **Use when:** Light-ground films.
- **Avoid when:** Dark grounds (use a cut).

### Stepped column fill

`tr-stepped-column-fill` · transitions · accent · energy medium · sting, launch, loop

Columns rise from the bottom edge in a stepped pyramid centred under the hero, spreading outward until they close into one solid field that becomes the next stage behind it.

- **Build:** Split the frame into N equal columns with no gutters, layered below the hero: 12-16 at 1920 px, or the hero's own grid unit so they line up with the bars or pixels of a mark. Column i starts d_i = |i − c| · 2 f after the first, where c is the column under the hero's centre. It rises from the bottom edge with height = H · prog(f, s + d_i, s + d_i + 40, E.smooth), so the tops form a stepped pyramid that widens outward. Fill each column with the next act's stage colour; in its full look every column carries a multi-hue vertical ramp. The columns are flat mask edges on a flat fill with nothing textured on them, so their tops may peak near 76 px/f. The hero keeps a living-hold creep throughout. Where the field rises behind it, draw a second copy of the hero in the opposite tone clipped to the union of the column rects (built by the same geometry function), so the hero flips tone exactly where a column stands behind it, with no fade. On the frame the outermost column fills, swap the column layer for one plate of that colour and land that frame on a downbeat. The hero answers it with scale 1 + 0.02 · hitPulse(f − close, 2, 5), or with its next build step.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Fill every column with one flat colour: the next stage colour, or the accent if this is the film's one accent flood. Or alternate two adjacent lightness steps of one hue from column to column and let them merge into a single tone as the field closes. Never put a ramp inside a column. The full look relies on gradient, orange, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Each column rises over 40 f on E.smooth (tops peak at about 76 px/f at 1080p). Stagger 2 f per column outward from the centre (7 steps for 14-15 columns), about 54 f in all. The field closes on a downbeat and swaps to one flat plate on the same frame. Hero pulse: attack 2 f, tau 5 f.
- **Use when:** Marks built from bars, steps or pixels; data and analytics products, where the columns read as a chart; stings and loop intros that change the stage colour behind a held hero.
- **Avoid when:** As a general scene change between unrelated shots (it reads as a preset blinds wipe), behind small readable type, or more than once per film.

### An object continues through the cut in a new role

`dv-object-carries-cut` · transitions · signature · energy medium · any

One element keeps moving across a hard cut and changes role on the other side: an avatar accelerating upward becomes the small header of a chat; a mark keeps shrinking while the background cuts; a finished line keeps breathing apart through the cut; a prompt card drifts up and jumps (+10.5 %) into a sent message bubble.

- **Build:** handoffShot(carry: ['x','y','k']) with the element drawn in both shots at the matched place; declare a velocity seam. Anatomy: Same screen position and speed on both sides (±20-30 px); scale may jump up to +10 % hidden by the cut. Sound: The cut on the beat (-27 ms); a footstep-like hit after. Materials: The logo icon survives the wipe: as a feathered white wipe erases the wordmark, the icon stays fully visible on top of the white for one frame, and on the next it is a small black glyph on a white tile already in its slot inside the new UI (a position jump of about 120 px).
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Materials:** The logo icon survives the wipe: as a feathered white wipe erases the wordmark, the icon stays fully visible on top of the white for one frame, and on the next it is a small black glyph on a white tile already in its slot inside the new UI (a position jump of about 120 px).
- **Timing:** Pre-cut 15-42 f ease-in; post-cut 23-89 f.
- **Use when:** Linking two states of the product; the brand mark entering the product.
- **Avoid when:** Changing the element's speed at the cut.

### Collapse to a dot relay

`tr-dot-relay` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

The hero collapses into one small dot, or the whole world shrinks into it. The dot, the only thing that survives, opens into the next object: a check ring, an avatar, the mark.

- **Build:** Collapse the hero (a card, a prompt box, or the detached dot of an i) to a 24-52 px dot: width and height go to the dot size and border-radius to 50%, over 4 f on E.in when it feeds a cut, or 16 f on E.out when it snaps and holds. To take the world with it, start 15 f later and scale the world group with k = lmix(1, 0.03, prog(f, s, s + 24, E.contact)) about the dot centre, over the next stage colour. Its corner radius grows to 50% and its mask edge is feathered 40 px; unmount it once it is smaller than the dot. The dot stays at full opacity through the seam (one absolute-frame function, or a hard cut that holds it on the same screen point). Then it opens into the next object: a check ring (stroke-dashoffset 1 → 0 and scale 0.6 → 1 over 8 f on E.out, its label 4 f later), an avatar disc (fill ramps paper → ink linearly over 12 f, icon fading in over the last 4 f), or the mark.
- **Timing:** Collapse: 4 f (E.in, into a cut) or 16 f (E.out, snap and hold). World shrink: 24 f on E.contact for a dot near centre (edges ≤ 66 px/f), or 40 f for a dot near a corner, starting 15 f after the collapse. Reopen over 8-12 f. Any device rotation that follows settles over 28 f on E.out.
- **Use when:** Submit, send, process, receive: actions that mean 'this went in and came out as that'. Also the film's signature device when the mark contains a dot.
- **Avoid when:** The dot would blink out or change size or colour at the seam, or the film already has an implosion seam.

### Exposure bloom into the next scene

`tr-exposure-bloom` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, update, vertical · also `dv-exposure-bloom`

The whole frame over-exposes on an accelerating curve (brightness plus a one-hue veil), the scenes hand over inside the light, and the next scene settles out of a small overshoot of its own brightness.

- **Build:** <Exposure frame at={hit} up down peak brightness swap={{ at, frames }} a={outgoing} b={incoming} />; a short charge pulse (charge) before it if the music has a pickup.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Exposure.Exposure`, `fx/Exposure.exposureState`
- **Timing:** Rise 40 f on E.buildIn, veil 0.82, brightness x1.5, the swap 10 f before the peak with a dissolve of at most 6 f under the light, settle 26 f on E.linear (the incoming scene peaks about 11 % over its rest in mean luma).
- **Use when:** A hit or a drop, into a reveal or a lockup; once or twice a film.
- **Avoid when:** The look is a light, white world already (there is no headroom: use a light sweep).

### Flat layout cuts into the same layout in the world

`dv-match-into-world` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A flat graphic layout pans (or the camera pushes toward a monitor) and cuts into real footage where the same layout is a street hoarding or the monitor's content full-frame: the design steps out into the world.

- **Build:** zoomThrough to the monitor's box then handoffShot; for the hoarding, match the layout's corners with a matrix3d onto the footage. Anatomy: Exit ease-in; the matched element at the same screen place on both sides; the cut can be silent. Sound: The cut on a beat with a boom; or a silent cut inside a silence.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Pre 42 f; post 145 f.
- **Use when:** Showing a design or a screen in use.
- **Avoid when:** Without footage that matches the layout's geometry.

### Giant word punch-out

`tr-giant-word-punch-out` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, sting, vertical, feature

A hard cut lands on an extreme close-up of an oversized word sliding fast and braking, its letters resolving one by one. A second cut jumps out to the whole word at reading size, arriving with wide tracking that slams together.

- **Build:** Close-up act: set the word at 2-2.5x its final size, cropped by the frame, with x = x_end + (x_start − x_end)·0.92^f, starting at no more than 70 px/f. Each letter animates blur 12 → 0 px and colour C.mute → C.ink over 12 f on a 2 f stagger starting at frame 4, so the first letter lands sharp at frame 16, when the pan is down to about 18 px/f. Cut on the act boundary while the word still moves at 13-20 px/f. Wide act: show the whole word, with p = prog(f, 0, 30, E.out) driving scale lmix(1.38, 1, p) and letter-spacing from 0.8 em to its resting track. Add a horizontal-only blur (SVG feGaussianBlur stdDeviation '18 0') set by blurIn(p, 18), opacity 0.5 → 1 over the first 8 f, and colour mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, t) with t going 0.6 → 1 over 17 f. Hold 30-60 f, then exit on E.in over 6-12 f.
- **Timing:** Close-up 18-22 f: starts at ≤ 70 px/f and slows ×0.92 per frame (about 18 px/f by frame 16); letters resolve over 12 f with a 2 f stagger from frame 4. Cut at 13-20 px/f residual speed. Wide entry 30 f on E.out: scale 1.38 → 1, tracking 0.8 em → rest, horizontal blur of 18 px gone by 60% of the move, outer letters ≤ 60 px/f. Colour settles in 17 f. Hold 30-60 f. Exit 6-12 f on E.in.
- **Use when:** A one-word claim or product name that deserves two beats: read it, then see it whole. Vertical cut-downs where one huge word fills the frame.
- **Avoid when:** Lines of more than two words, or words over about 10 letters (the close-up loses the word); or when the next shot needs the word small within a second.

### Glitch run: distinct full-frame looks on twos

`dv-glitch-state-run` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, sting

A break out of live action in four completely different full-frame looks, each held exactly two frames, alternating bright and dark: a ghost smear with channel split, a blue block mosaic with the subject inverted, a scan-line displacement tear, a black frame with the caption collapsed into a streak; or a posterised 1-bit capture flash for four frames that breaks up.

- **Build:** Recipe: a sequencer of 2-frame looks, each its own layer: offset copies, a Pixelate block level, seeded horizontal strips, a black frame with a scaleY streak. Anatomy: States held 2 f each; luma high-low-high-low (139, 29, 117, 4); bands 10-40 px tall with seeded offsets. Sound: Starts on the end of the spoken phrase; a shutter hit on the capture.
- **Timing:** 4 states x 5 f (20 f); posterise 8 f + 4 f break.
- **Use when:** Tearing the viewer from realism into the graphic world, once, on the end of a spoken phrase.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films; more than once; gradual blending between states.

### Over-exposed frame with a negative ghost

`dv-flash-ghost-cut` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, feature, sting

After a whip on an ease-in, one frame at about 92 % white carries a blurred grey negative ghost of the outgoing object, then one dark streak frame, then the next shot sliding in.

- **Build:** <FlashCut whip flash streak slide pull> (smear 'draw', house: the whip's tail and the slide's head streak). Anatomy: Whip ease-in; flash 0.92 with a 0.3 ghost; one streak frame; slide in 28 f, most smeared on its first frames, and pull back. Sound: On the swell peak.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.FlashCut`
- **Timing:** Flash 2 f.
- **Use when:** A whip transition on a swell's peak.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films.

### Pixel glint sprite on twos bridges a cut

`dv-glint-sprite-bridge` · transitions · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

Right after a hard cut, a tiny cluster of 3-4 bright squares (about 66, 53 and 24 px) drops diagonally across the frame, changing its arrangement every 2 frames through six poses (diagonal triplet, tall bar + square + dot, wide block + tick, two bars + dot in an L, a long bar with dots above and below, a single square), then vanishes; the new scene rises behind it on ones while the stage flashes and decays.

- **Build:** Build: <Glint at x y color> (fx/Glint) on the first frame after the cut: six poses of 1-3 squares, a new pose every 4 f at 60 fps (on twos at 30), dropping down-right along a 330 px path; flip mirrors it; glintGlow(f, at) gives the stage flash (half gone in one 30 fps frame, then a 30 f tail). Anatomy: A pose table of rects in local px; the group travels a slightly accelerating path (about 34 px per pose); each square with a soft halo; stage glow to luma 36 then a decay over 30 f. Sound: A whip whoosh into the cut.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Glint`
- **Conditions:** light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo
- **Timing:** 6 poses x 4 f at 60 fps (on twos at 30) = 24 f; path 340 px.
- **Use when:** A cut that needs a bridge with character: from a send action to the result, into a new scene on a whip.
- **Avoid when:** Glows on light grounds; using it more than twice per film.

### Three single frames with an inverted centre band

`dv-inverted-band-separator` · transitions · signature · energy high · launch, loop

A loop resets through three one-frame images (the product UI, the key word huge, scattered tiles), each with its centre band (about 56 % of the width) colour-inverted while the outer strips stay normal; then the main shot returns.

- **Build:** Build: <InvertBand at count={3} sources={[a, b, c]}> (fx/Flashes): each source one beat (2 f at 60), with an inverted copy clipped to the centre 56 % band; every image a declared flash. Anatomy: A fixed vertical band applying invert over three different sources, one frame each. Sound: None needed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Flashes.InvertBand`
- **Timing:** 3 x 2 f; repeats every 104 f in a loop.
- **Use when:** A loop separator; a beat between sections in a playful film.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per loop.

### Defocus pulse that hides a jump

`cam-defocus-pulse-hide` · camera · accent · energy calm · feature, loop · also `dv-defocus-pulse-hide`

The whole frame goes soft and comes back in a third of a second; on the softest frame the camera's scale jumps, and nobody sees it. The hero stays sharp above the blur.

- **Build:** defocusPulse({ at, frames, peakSigma, scaleJump, fps })(f) gives { sigma, k }: multiply your camera's k by k and draw the world with <RackFocus t={sigma / peakSigma} blur={peakSigma} levels hero={...} />, so the blur is two copies at fixed radii and the hero (the product, the word) is drawn outside the stack.
- **Primitive:** `fx/SnapZoom.defocusPulse`, `fx/RackFocus`
- **Materials:** A whole-frame blur of about 3, 6, 3 px across the cut (last wide frame, first close-up frame, the next), sharp after: 8 f in all, with no exposure change.
- **Timing:** 18 f (17-19) from first blur to sharp, peak 20 px@1080 at the middle, scale jump x1.24 (x1.22-1.36) on the peak frame. Below 1 px of blur a frame still reads sharp and above 2 px it already reads fully soft, so shape the first and last few frames. At most one pulse every 0.4-1.3 s.
- **Use when:** A one-take film that needs a reframe or a size change without a cut; the kick of the music.
- **Avoid when:** Text must be read during the pulse.

### Vertical drum swap with a heat and a tilt

`dv-drum-swap` · typography in motion · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Before each swap the word heats in colour, tilts away like a drum face and exits up while the next word (or icon tile) enters from below; the last one flattens and exits.

- **Build:** MaskRise in + an exit with rotateX(-60deg) and rise; colour via HueSweep back. Anatomy: Heat 23 f, rotateX tilt on exit, entry from below. Sound: Plucks on the swaps; a shutter on the last.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MaskRise`
- **Timing:** Heat 23 f; exit 20 f; entry 23-25 f; final flatten 10 f.
- **Use when:** A list of sources or places in one sentence ("from Phone / Folders / Drives").
- **Avoid when:** More than three swaps.

### An empty beat before the logo

`dv-empty-beat` · pacing and structure · accent · energy calm · launch, sting

After the last phrase blurs out, the frame stays empty (just the ground and its light) for about three quarters of a second before the logo arrives.

- **Build:** A gap in the timeline with the LightField still running. Anatomy: Ground only, light field alive. Sound: Quiet.
- **Timing:** 45 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** Before the end card.
- **Avoid when:** Longer than about 1 s; a dead black frame without the ground's light.
